queue_items.claim: The row's sole rear-seam driver is carried entirely by the WEB rendering of the seam verse: no oshb ref or pointed splice stands at Isa.66.18, and the English run the row quotes supplies a verb the MT does not have.
queue_items.grounds: boundary_evidence_refs lists web:Isa.66.18-Isa.66.18 with no oshb counterpart, and the warrant reads that 66:18 'opens with a first-person emphatic pivot' evidenced only by “For I know their works and their thoughts.” (web:Isa.66.18). MT 66:18 opens "וְאָנֹכִ֗י מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם֙ וּמַחְשְׁבֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם בָּאָ֕ה" (oshb:Isa.66.18, byte tier): no verb governs 'their works and their thoughts' -- "בָּאָ֕ה" (oshb:Isa.66.18, byte tier) is the 3fs predicate of the gathering clause that follows -- so WEB's 'know' is a translator's supply and WEB's 'For' renders the waw of "וְאָנֹכִ֗י" (oshb:Isa.66.18, byte tier). The pivot claim is nonetheless byte-true, since "וְאָנֹכִ֗י" is the verse-initial emphatic 1cs independent pronoun, so the seam itself survives re-derivation; only the shipped warrant is translation-dependent. Tier-4/engagement-class defect, not a byte-false claim.
queue_items.proposed_change: Add "oshb:Isa.66.18-Isa.66.18" to boundary_evidence_refs and carry the pivot on a pointed splice of the verse-initial "וְאָנֹכִ֗י" at byte tier, retaining the WEB run as rendering only. No span change.

queue_items.claim: The front-seam onset run the row splices itself opens with a backward-linking connective, a byte-true continuity signal across the row's own Isa.66.14|Isa.66.15 seam that the row neither discloses nor rebuts.
queue_items.grounds: MT 66:15 opens "כִּֽי הִנֵּ֤ה" (oshb:Isa.66.15, byte tier); the leading "כִּֽי" subordinates the theophany announcement to the immediately preceding clause "וְזָעַ֖ם אֶת אֹיְבָֽיו" (oshb:Isa.66.14, byte tier), and 66:16 chains a second connective of the same form, "כִּ֤י בָאֵשׁ֙" (oshb:Isa.66.16, byte tier). The row splices the connective inside its onset run and glosses it 'for behold', then argues the run purely as an onset; the continuity force of the connective at the row's own front seam is never disclosed, which the cross-seam cohesion rule requires. The seam is still defensible on the presentative and the subject/register change, so no merge is proposed.
queue_items.proposed_change: Add a one-clause disclosure to device_notes or strongest_rejected_alternative acknowledging the backward force of the connective opening 66:15 and stating why the presentative onset and the subject shift override it. No span change.

queue_items.claim: confidence 'high' does not survive the row's own evidence.
queue_items.grounds: The rear seam carries no original-language evidence at the seam verse and the front seam carries an undisclosed byte-level continuity signal, both under a 'high' band; the neighbour row spanning Isa.66.12-Isa.66.14 carries the identical Isa.66.14|Isa.66.15 seam on the same theophany-onset driver at 'medium'. The row's own span is not a whole chapter, so the chapter-fallback cap is not what is at issue -- the band simply outruns the warrants as shipped.
queue_items.proposed_change: Reduce confidence to 'medium'. Dependent on the two seam-warrant remedies above: if both are repaired, the band may be re-opened rather than fixed at medium.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A theophany announcement opens the unit, "כִּֽי הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בָּאֵ֣שׁ יָב֔וֹא" (oshb:Isa.66.15, byte tier) (web:Isa.66.15, 'for behold, Yahweh will come with fire'), rendered “For, behold, Yahweh will come with fire, and his chariots will be like the whirlwind” (web:Isa.66.15), a register shift from the maternal-comfort imagery of the preceding unit into universal judgment “on all flesh” (web:Isa.66.16). It closes at the indictment of those who eat forbidden food in the gardens, ending on the divine-speech signature "נְאֻם יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Isa.66.17, byte tier) (web:Isa.66.17, 'says Yahweh'; this verse also carries a ketiv/qere note, disclosed below). The unit ends there because 66:18 opens with a first-person emphatic pivot, “For I know their works and their thoughts.” (web:Isa.66.18), shifting the subject from judgment on apostates to the ingathering of the nations.
boundary_evidence_refs: web:Isa.66.17-Isa.66.17 (ketiv/qere note, single-witness; the row does not adjudicate the variant)
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through the following ingathering material as one continuous 'universal reckoning' oracle was considered, since both concern the nations; it is rejected because 66:17 closes on its own divine-speech signature ('says Yahweh') and 66:18 opens with a first-person pivot introducing a distinct action (gathering the nations to see Yahweh's glory) rather than continuing the fire-judgment announcement.

shipped_row.device_notes: The disclosure inventory records a ketiv/qere note at Isa.66.17 (single-witness; the row takes no position on the reading). No petuchah/setumah mark falls at this unit's front-seam (Isa.66.14) or its own span, so the boundaries rest on tier-1 signals alone.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A koh-amar frame reopens the comfort oracle, "כִּֽי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה" (oshb:Isa.66.12, byte tier) (web:Isa.66.12, 'for thus says Yahweh'), rendered “Behold, I will extend peace to her like a river, and the glory of the nations like an overflowing stream” (web:Isa.66.12). It develops the same nursing/comforting-mother imagery through “As one whom his mother comforts, so I will comfort you.” (web:Isa.66.13) and closes at “Yahweh's hand will be known among his servants; and he will have indignation against his enemies.” (web:Isa.66.14). The unit ends there because 66:15 opens a new theophany announcement, “For, behold, Yahweh will come with fire” (web:Isa.66.15), a different register (judgment theophany rather than maternal comfort).

next_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens on a first-person emphatic pivot, “For I know their works and their thoughts. The time comes that I will gather all nations and languages” (web:Isa.66.18), moving the subject from judgment on apostates to a universal ingathering: survivors sent to far-off nations (66:19), all Israel's brothers brought as an offering (66:20), priests and Levites selected even from among them (66:21). It closes on a permanence assurance echoing the new-creation declaration of 65:17 as a lexical collocation differing in determination -- "שָׁמַ֥יִם חֲדָשִׁ֖ים וָאָ֣רֶץ חֲדָשָׁ֑ה" (oshb:Isa.65.17, indefinite, byte tier) against "הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם הַ֠חֳדָשִׁים וְהָאָ֨רֶץ הַחֲדָשָׁ֜ה" (oshb:Isa.66.22, definite, byte tier) (web:Isa.66.22, 'the new heavens and the new earth') -- each four-token run standing in exactly 1 verse book-wide, the two collating against each other at no tier. The postpositive pair "נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה" (oshb:Isa.66.22, byte tier) ('says Yahweh') stands mid-verse, at tokens 12-13 of 17, carrying the verse's own major dividing accent, with four further tokens -- "כֵּ֛ן יַעֲמֹ֥ד זַרְעֲכֶ֖ם וְשִׁמְכֶֽם" (oshb:Isa.66.22, byte tier) -- completing the comparison opened earlier in the same verse by "כִּ֣י כַאֲשֶׁ֣ר" (oshb:Isa.66.22, byte tier); it does not seal the unit. The unit ends there because 66:23 opens a new temporal formula ('from one new moon to another') describing recurring worship rather than the one-time ingathering event.

queue_items.claim: The couplet's stated cohesion warrant does not bind Isa.66.23 to Isa.66.24 against the verse-final closure-class signal the row itself computes at 66:23, and the closure test the neighbouring row applies is satisfied at this internal juncture but never run.
queue_items.grounds: The row gives two reasons for holding the couplet: that 'it is the book's terminal span (no rear seam follows 66:24)' -- a tiling fact, not a cohesion signal -- and that the couplet's internal turn 'is a distinct rhetorical function from the ingathering report that precedes it', which distinguishes the couplet from what precedes rather than binding its two verses to each other. Against them: MT 66:23 closes on "אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Isa.66.23, byte tier), re-swept as verse-final in exactly 5 verses book-wide (sweep: 5 verses, skeleton tier; Isa.39.6, Isa.54.1, Isa.65.25, Isa.66.21, Isa.66.23, word-bound at all five) -- the row's own digit, confirmed; and MT 66:24 opens on a fresh scene with a new subject and setting, "וְיָצְא֣וּ וְרָא֔וּ" (oshb:Isa.66.24, byte tier). The neighbouring row spanning Isa.66.18-Isa.66.22 rejects a seam at a verse-final speech signature only because 'no addressee, frame, or scene shift of its own' accompanies it; that test's second limb is met at 66:23|66:24, and this row never applies it. The frontier flag holds the coda-versus-close question open but does not test the seam, and the two verses are not one sentence, so the syntactic-continuity protection does not reach them.
queue_items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY, for adjudication -- either (a) split into Isa.66.23-Isa.66.23 (the recurring-worship formula closing on its verse-final speech signature) and Isa.66.24-Isa.66.24 (the terminal judgment image), or (b) retain Isa.66.23-Isa.66.24 and supply a positive cohesion warrant that survives the verse-final closure signal at 66:23 and the scene shift at 66:24, replacing the terminal-span tiling fact. Under (a) the over-split risk of two single-verse terminal rows must be weighed, and unit_type, confidence and the rejected alternative re-open as dependent fields.

queue_items.claim: The book-wide 'all-flesh collocation' digit counts a skeleton substring rather than the collocation it names: it includes a site that is not the collocation and excludes an attested one.
queue_items.grounds: Shipped: '(sweep: 3 verses in this chapter, 6 book-wide, skeleton tier)'. Re-swept, the skeleton substring underlying "כָל בָּשָׂ֛ר" (oshb:Isa.66.23, byte tier) returns 6 verses -- Isa.22.13, Isa.40.5, Isa.49.26, Isa.66.16, Isa.66.23, Isa.66.24. The Isa.22.13 hit falls across "אָכֹ֥ל בָּשָׂ֖ר" (oshb:Isa.22.13, byte tier), 'eat meat', where the substring spans the tail of the infinitive and the following noun and is not the all-flesh collocation at all; and the articular all-flesh site "כָּל הַבָּשָׂ֣ר" (oshb:Isa.40.6, byte tier) is excluded because its skeleton carries the article. The head word is a two-letter function word, the short-token class the hazard catalog requires word-binding for before any digit. The in-chapter digit re-verifies exactly (3 verses: Isa.66.16, Isa.66.23, Isa.66.24). Not load-bearing for either seam -- it supports the held coda question.
queue_items.proposed_change: Restate the book-wide digit with its object named -- either keep 6 and disclose it as a skeleton-substring census including the 'eat meat' site at 22:13, or count the collocation proper and disclose the articular site at 40:6 separately. The in-chapter digit stands as shipped.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens with a recurring-time formula distinct from the one-time ingathering event of the preceding unit, “It shall happen that from one new moon to another, and from one Sabbath to another, all flesh will come to worship before me,” (web:Isa.66.23), rendered in Hebrew as "יָב֧וֹא כָל בָּשָׂ֛ר לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֥ת" (oshb:Isa.66.23, byte tier) ('all flesh will come to worship'), closing that same verse, “says Yahweh” (web:Isa.66.23), rendering "אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Isa.66.23, byte tier) -- a verse-final speech signature whose contiguous pair stands in 53 verses book-wide and verse-final in only 5 (sweep: 5 verses, skeleton tier), a byte fact this couplet's own held question weighs, not resolves. The book's very last verse turns from that universal worship to a grim closing image, “They will go out, and look at the dead bodies of the men who have transgressed against me; for their worm will not die, nor will their fire be quenched” (web:Isa.66.24), rendered "תוֹלַעְתָּ֞ם לֹ֣א תָמ֗וּת" (oshb:Isa.66.24, byte tier) ('their worm will not die'). This couplet is kept as its own unit because it is the book's terminal span (no rear seam follows 66:24) and because its own internal turn -- from universal worship to unending punishment of the transgressors -- is a distinct rhetorical function from the ingathering report that precedes it.
boundary_evidence_refs: web:Isa.66.22-Isa.66.22 (front-seam of this unit is unmarked; cited for tiling)
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping this couplet fused to the preceding ingathering unit as one larger span was considered, since no formal header or vocative separates 66:22 from 66:23, and 66:23 opens on a connective-prefixed temporal continuation, "וְהָיָ֗ה" (oshb:Isa.66.23, byte tier), attested verse-initially in 50 verses book-wide (sweep: 50 verses, skeleton tier) -- a form that distinguishes nothing at this seam by itself; it is rejected here because 66:23's recurring new-moon-and-Sabbath formula reports a standing liturgical order rather than continuing the one-time gathering narrated earlier in the chapter, a content distinction rather than a tier-1 form marker, which is why this row sits at reduced confidence rather than a higher band. Whether 66:24 functions as this oracle's own conclusion or as a coda to the whole book is held open from Isaiah's own text and not adjudicated here.

shipped_row.device_notes: Held at medium_low confidence and flagged as a genuine frontier question: the tonal turn between universal worship (66:23) and the undying-worm image (66:24) is a recognized crux this row observes from the bytes without resolving, and no petuchah/setumah mark falls within this closing span to corroborate either reading. The all-flesh collocation itself spans the couplet and reaches beyond it: "כָל בָּשָׂ֛ר" (oshb:Isa.66.23, byte tier) stands inside this row's own first verse, "לְכָל בָּשָֽׂר" (oshb:Isa.66.24, byte tier) closes it verse-finally, and the chapter's third site stands at "כָּל בָּשָׂ֑ר" (oshb:Isa.66.16, byte tier) (sweep: 3 verses in this chapter, 6 book-wide, skeleton tier) -- so the held coda-versus-close question carries byte evidence on both sides. This span closes the book; no rear seam follows Isa.66.24.
